newsitem.title: USA: Ford to bring Cougar back in 1999 model year.
newsitem.headline: Ford to bring Cougar back in 1999 model year.

text.p: The Mercury Cougar is coming back, Ford Motor Co. said Tuesday, this time as a smaller front-wheel-drive coupe that officials predicted will steal sales from imports and invigorate the Mercury brand.

Ford Automotive President Jacques Nasser said the new Cougar will appear in the 1999 model year in both the United States and Europe. Analysts have said production of the car will start in August 1998 at Ford's Flat Rock, Mich., AutoAlliance venture, with retail sales beginning in October.
Ford announced in March that the old Cougar, an ageing rear-wheel drive two-door plagued by slow sales, would be discontinued this year, along with three other vehicles.

Based on the same Mondeo platform used for the Contour and Mystique small cars, the new Cougar is slightly larger than the Ford Probe, which is also being killed off. It will be be offered with both a six-cylinder and four-cylinder engine.

James O'Connor, general manager of Mercury, said U.S. sales volume will be more than 50,000 cars a year. Ford expects sales to come from existing Probe and Cougar customers, although the majority are seen coming from imports.

Ford officials would not reveal prices for the new Cougar or how much it is costing to develop. Nasser noted that a car designed from an existing platform and powertrain can shave up to one-third off its development time.

The Cougar will only be sold under the Mercury brand in the United States. As such, it will be the first vehicle to give a new image to Mercury, which has long suffered under the shadow of its sister Ford division.
Ford is positioning Mercury as a division that offers "fun, flair and flexibility" and attracts a broader, younger range of customers.
"That means offering vehicles that are a little bit different than the mainstream vehicles, offering vehicles with a little more style, maybe a little more edge," Nasser said.
Although the market for coupes has been dwindling for years, Nasser said Ford sees the new Cougar as filling a niche in the growing small speciality segment.

On Tuesday, Ford officials unveiled a Mercury concept car called the MC2 that they said shows the design cues the new Cougar will have. The unveiling occurred at the Concours d'Elegance classic car show at Meadow Brook Hall in Rochester, Mich. Employing what automotive designers call the "New Edge"
look, the MC2's resembles the MC4 Ford showed at the North American International Auto Show in Detroit.

The exterior is made up of sculpted body panels joined by crisp edges. The MC2 seats four people. Interior features include a swiveling panel with the entertainment system controls and climate control knobs similar to rotary telephone dials that are easy to grip.
